title: Python: an implicit dunder's instance write must not refuse the call (N6 recall follow-up, DEC-303 a80)
description: Record-only ORDINARY follow-up (not held) from DEC-303 (a80) (opum-ai/opum-doc#2083, ODOC-640), reviewer N6's over-refusal half. In GCLI-140's attribute-write rule, a write to self.__call__ (or another implicit dunder) makes x() unresolved, but implicit special methods are looked up on the TYPE, never the instance dict, so the instance write should not refuse the call. This is RECALL, not a wrong edge, so it is separate from the held GCLI-151. Measure the shape first (class C with def __call__; a method writing self.__call__ = f; x = C(); x()): if the site refuses, the fix is to exempt the implicit dunder names from the instance-write guard, with a red-before/green-after fixture and a mutant; if it does not refuse, the task closes with the measurement. The held half (N6's missed C.__init__ refusal) stays in GCLI-151.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The measured shape is recorded: whether self.__call__ = f refuses x() on the current head
If it refuses, an implicit dunder (__call__, __len__, __iter__, __enter__, ...) written on an instance no longer refuses the dunder call, with a red-before/green-after fixture and a mutant
No other refusal changes: the five-pin delta is identical apart from the named sites
